The retailer also said Old Navy's turnaround is showing signs of progress, sending shares up more than 11% Friday.

Kechter comes to Gap from activewear retailer Vuori, where she was global president and oversaw the brand's global business strategy, marketing and financials. She was previously global brand president of Fabletics and began her career at Gap before that.

"I'm excited to return to Gap Inc. and partner with [Gap CEO Richard Dickson] and the team to strengthen our connection with customers and shape the brand's next chapter," Kechter said in a statement.

The announcement comes after Lululemon poached former Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger to be its chief product officer last month.

In a recent development, "Clearly, we're disappointed with Athleta's performance, and we recognize there's a lot of work ahead," Dickson told CNBC. "We had been in rebuild mode, but now we're really in turnaround mode.".

It has been revealed that dickson remarked the tech giant is focused on getting back to its fundamentals: fabrications, feature, form, function and fit. Dickson added that Kechter will be conducting a "comprehensive review" of the brand to reposition Athleta for future success.

While the execution of its strategy has thus far "fallen short," Dickson mentioned this new approach will allow Athleta to fully realize its potential.

According to recent reports, gap also reported mixed fiscal third-quarter earnings on Thursday and posted flat overall comparable sales. Wall Street had been expecting a comparable sales increase of 1.3%, according to StreetAccount.

Net sales grew 2%, though demand softened in October and early November due to warmer weather, the firm mentioned. Store sales increased 1%, while online sales increased 3%.

Gap also said it's recorded a $420 million adjustment to cost of goods sold and a $21 million adjustment to interest income from tariff refunds so far this year.

In a recent development, the company lowered its full-year net sales outlook to be "roughly flat," down from previous guidance of up between 1% and 1.5%. Gap is also now expecting adjusted earnings per share of between $2.29 and $2.34, down from an earlier expectation of between $2.35 and $2.45 per share.

Dickson remarked in an interview that much of the lowered guidance was due to warmer weather in the first two weeks of the quarter, but he said Gap is expecting "meaningful acceleration" in shopping ahead of the peak holiday season.

"We're monitoring the trends, and we're going to remain agile as we respond to the changing business trends," Dickson stated.

Here's how the organization performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

According to recent reports, for the quarter, Gap reported net income of $311 million, or 86 cents per share, compared with $236 million, or 62 cents per share, the year prior. Sales rose slightly from $3.94 billion the year prior.

According to recent reports, at Athleta, net sales were down 14% compared with last year, coming in at $220 million. Comparable sales for the banner sank 15%, which the manufacturer attributed to "limited traction" from efforts to modernize its merchandise and marketing. `.

Sources indicate that the manufacturer's namesake brand saw 9% comparable sales growth for the quarter, with net sales of $1.1 billion, marking an 11% increase compared with last year. Dickson noted it was the brand's 12th consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales.

"Gap is really firing on all cylinders, and the consistency of the brand is really giving us confidence in the brand's ability to continue its momentum," Dickson said.

It has been revealed that the Old Navy banner saw flat comparable sales for the quarter and net sales of $2.3 billion, up 1% compared with last year. It's the first earnings report since the brand, which has been experiencing sluggish sales, named Michael Francis as its new CEO last quarter. Francis began his role at Old Navy on Nov. 2.

In a recent development, banana Republic saw its net sales sink 3% compared with last year, which the manufacturer attributed to delayed demand for cold-weather categories and a women's fall assortment that fell flat. Wall Street had been expecting growth of 1.5%, according to StreetAccount.

Dickson remarked the brand has since introduced new products and seen demand "rebound" as cooler weather has set in across the country.

"We've been encouraged by the early customer response, and we should see sequential improvement in the fourth quarter," he remarked. "There's some work to do here, but with peak selling still ahead, I'm confident that the team is focused on the right areas and [will] ultimately position Banana well for growth.".

#81881. Even scientists can't agree on what science actually is

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (789 w)

Even scientists can't agree on what science actually is

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, scientists dedicate their careers to uncovering how the world works, yet they have surprisingly different opinions about what science actually means.
  • Sources indicate that the study, published in Royal Society Open Science, examined 18 different descriptions of science and found that researchers rarely embraced any of them without reservations.
  • "What was surprising to me was that there was quite a bit of disagreement between scientists, including scientists who are in the same subfield," says Marina Dubova, who led the research while working as a postdoctoral researcher at the Santa Fe Institute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, scientists dedicate their careers to uncovering how the world works, yet they have surprisingly different opinions about what science actually means. Latest research reveals that scientists disagree about the nature and purpose of science even more than the general public does.

Sources indicate that the study, published in Royal Society Open Science, examined 18 different descriptions of science and found that researchers rarely embraced any of them without reservations. Even when scientists generally supported a particular definition, many questioned some aspect of it.

"What was surprising to me was that there was quite a bit of disagreement between scientists, including scientists who are in the same subfield," says Marina Dubova, who led the research while working as a postdoctoral researcher at the Santa Fe Institute.

Members of the public, by comparison, expressed more consistent views. They were more likely to regard science as a dependable way to discover objective truths about the world, placing less importance on the uncertainty and creativity involved in scientific research.

Recent findings suggest that these contrasting perspectives may have vital consequences. They could affect the questions scientists choose to investigate and influence how people evaluate scientific findings. They may also help explain why the public sometimes becomes frustrated when researchers cannot offer clear answers or change their conclusions in response to new evidence.

What Scientists and the Public Believe About Science.

Dubova, now an assistant professor of psychology at the University of California, Berkeley, worked with Princeton University researcher Qiawen E. Liu to investigate how people understand science.

Industry observers note that the researchers surveyed 91 scientists and 99 members of the public. Participants were asked to assess 18 descriptions of science drawn from historical perspectives, including comparisons of scientific research to detective work, a pursuit of truth, and a mirror that reflects reality.

Sources indicate that both groups generally agreed that curiosity, exploration, and the desire to solve mysteries are central to science. Beyond those shared ideas, however, the scientists expressed strikingly different perspectives.

Some researchers viewed science primarily as a means of discovering objective truths. Others placed greater importance on imagination, personal judgment, and the creative decisions involved in research. Scientists also differed over whether scientific progress depends mainly on following established procedures or adapting and improvising as upcoming challenges arise.

Dubova believes these disagreements may reflect the individual experiences that shape how researchers approach their work. Just as chefs can have very different philosophies about preparing food, scientists can develop distinct ideas about the best ways to investigate the world.

Why the Public Sees Science Differently.

According to recent reports, another intriguing finding involved differences among scientific disciplines. The general public's understanding of science more closely resembled the views expressed by physicists and biologists than those of psychologists and other social scientists.

One possible reason is that physics and biology receive greater attention in science education, potentially shaping how people imagine scientific research. Dubova emphasizes, however, that this explanation remains tentative and will require additional investigation.

The differences between scientists and the public could also help explain misunderstandings about scientific uncertainty. People who expect science to produce firm, objective answers may have difficulty understanding why findings sometimes conflict or why scientific conclusions must be updated when upcoming evidence becomes available.

What the Findings Could Mean for AI and Scientific Discovery.

The research also points to a potential challenge as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly involved in scientific discovery.

With researchers developing AI systems that can carry out scientific investigations, Dubova is concerned that automation could favor a limited conception of how science should work. If those systems are built around one particular approach to research, other valuable methods of discovery could receive less attention.

According to recent reports, the study received support from the Santa Fe Institute's Lou Schuyler Seed Grant Fund, which was created in 2022 to encourage exploratory projects by early career scientists. Dubova used the funding to pay participants for taking part in the research.

For Dubova, the findings represent an initial effort to understand how scientists' underlying beliefs about their profession might influence the research they conduct and the discoveries they make.

"Don't take the common understanding of science for granted," she says. "Always ask. Always be curious about what someone has in mind.".

According to recent reports, materials provided by Santa Fe Institute. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China on Tuesday unveiled the crew for this week's Shenzhou-24 space mission, with a Pakistani payload specialist set to become the first foreign astronaut to board its Tiangong space station.

According to recent reports, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) mentioned that Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a 40-year-old former Pakistani air force pilot, would join two Chinese colleagues when the mission rolls out from the Jiuquan launch center in China's northwestern Gobi Desert at 8:18 a.m. local time (0018 GMT)  on Wednesday.

"I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a news conference on Tuesday, switching between Urdu, Mandarin and English.

"To every child who is watching while I'm in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams," he said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pakistani officials welcomed Ali's selection as a significant milestone in relations between Islamabad and Beijing who are this year marking 75 years of cooperation in space.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the mission as a "source of joy and pride for the entire nation" and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the mission underscored the "iron brotherhood" between the two countries.

"This mission is not a finish line; I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut and one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon, to Mars, and beyond," remarked Ali.

"Together with my Chinese crew mates, I will show that this friendship is real, not only on paper, but also in orbit.".

Recent findings suggest that ali will not be the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar explorer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023. But he will be the first foreign astronaut to join a Chinese mission.

During a short orbital flight expected to last around five days, Ali will carry out a series of experiments in the fields of biotechnology and photosynthetic microorganisms before returning to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked at the Tiangong in May.

In a recent development, china has poured billions of dollars into its space program. Its prized Tiangong space station is stewarded by teams of three astronauts that are typically rotated every six months.

Beijing is aiming to land Chinese astronauts on the moon for the first time by 2030 and is seen as the main space rival to the United States, which is hoping to return to the lunar surface in 2028.

#81879. Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

📅 02 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1924 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNN ↗ Open Full Page

Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

📅 02 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1924 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is one of China’s most popular shopping apps, selling clothing, groceries and just about everything else under the sun to more than 750 million consumers a month.
  • But according to cybersecurity researchers, it can also bypass people’ cell phone security to monitor activities on other apps, check notifications, read private messages and change settings.
  • While many apps collect vast troves of user data, sometimes without explicit consent, experts say e-commerce giant Pinduoduo has taken violations of privacy and data security to the next level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is one of China’s most popular shopping apps, selling clothing, groceries and just about everything else under the sun to more than 750 million consumers a month.

But according to cybersecurity researchers, it can also bypass people’ cell phone security to monitor activities on other apps, check notifications, read private messages and change settings.

And once installed, it’s tough to remove.

While many apps collect vast troves of user data, sometimes without explicit consent, experts say e-commerce giant Pinduoduo has taken violations of privacy and data security to the next level.

In a detailed investigation, CNN spoke to half a dozen cybersecurity teams from Asia, Europe and the United States — as well as multiple former and current Pinduoduo employees — after receiving a tipoff.

Sources indicate that multiple experts identified the presence of malware on the Pinduoduo app that exploited vulnerabilities in Android operating systems. Company insiders said the exploits were utilized to spy on customers and competitors, allegedly to boost sales.

“We haven’t seen a mainstream app like this trying to escalate their privileges to gain access to things that they’re not supposed to gain access to,” noted Mikko Hyppönen, chief research officer at WithSecure, a Finnish cybersecurity firm.

“This is highly unusual, and it is pretty damning for Pinduoduo.”.

Malware, short for malicious software, refers to any software developed to steal data or interfere with computer systems and mobile devices.

Evidence of sophisticated malware in the Pinduoduo app comes amid intense scrutiny of Chinese-developed apps like TikTok over concerns about data security.

Some American lawmakers are pushing for a national ban on the popular short-video app, whose CEO Shou Chew was grilled by Congress for five hours last week about its relations with the Chinese government.

The revelations are also likely to draw more attention to Pinduoduo’s international sister app, Temu, which is topping US download charts and fast expanding in other Western markets. Both are owned by Nasdaq-listed PDD, a multinational company with roots in China.

While Temu has not been implicated, Pinduoduo’s alleged actions risk casting a shadow over its sister app’s global expansion.

It has been revealed that there is no evidence that Pinduoduo has handed data to the Chinese government. But as Beijing enjoys significant leverage over businesses under its jurisdiction, there are concerns from US lawmakers that any organization operating in China could be forced to cooperate with a broad range of security activities.

The findings follow Google’s suspension of Pinduoduo from its Play Store in March, citing malware identified in versions of the app.

An ensuing report from Bloomberg stated a Russian cybersecurity firm had also identified potential malware in the app.

Pinduoduo has previously rejected “the speculation and accusation that Pinduoduo app is malicious.”.

CNN has contacted PDD multiple times over email and phone for comment, but has not received a response.

Pinduoduo, which boasts a user base that accounts for three quarters of China’s online population and a market value three times that of eBay (EBAY), wasn’t always an online shopping behemoth.

Founded in 2015 in Shanghai by Colin Huang, a former Google employee, the startup was fighting to establish itself in a market long dominated by e-commerce stalwarts Alibaba (BABA) and JD.com (JD).

It succeeded by offering steep discounts on friends-and-family group buying orders and focusing on lower-income rural areas.

Sources indicate that pinduoduo posted triple digit growth in monthly users until the end of 2018, the year it listed in Upcoming York. By the middle of 2020, though, the increase in monthly users had slowed to around 50% and would continue to decline, according to its earnings reports.

It was in 2020, according to a current Pinduoduo employee, that the tech giant set up a team of about 100 engineers and product managers to dig for vulnerabilities in Android phones, develop ways to exploit them — and turn that into profit.

According to the source, who requested anonymity for fear of reprisals, the company only targeted users in rural areas and smaller towns initially, while avoiding users in megacities such as Beijing and Shanghai.

“The goal was to reduce the risk of being exposed,” they remarked.

By collecting expansive data on user activities, the manufacturer was able to create a comprehensive portrait of people’ habits, interests and preferences, according to the source.

This allowed it to improve its machine learning model to offer more personalized push notifications and ads, attracting customers to open the app and place orders, they mentioned.

The team was disbanded in early March, the source added, after questions about their activities came to light.

PDD didn’t reply to CNN’s repeated requests for comment on the team.

Approached by CNN, researchers from Tel Aviv-based cyber firm Check Point Research, Delaware-based app security startup Oversecured and Hyppönen’s WithSecure conducted independent analysis of the 6.49.0 version of the app, released on Chinese app stores in late February.

Sources indicate that google Play is not available in China, and Android users in the country download their apps from local stores. In March, when Google suspended Pinduoduo, it stated it had found malware in off-Play versions of the app.

The researchers found code designed to achieve “privilege escalation”: a type of cyberattack that exploits a vulnerable operating system to gain a higher level of access to data than it’s supposed to have, according to experts.

“Our team has reverse engineered that code and we can confirm that it tries to escalate rights, tries to gain access to things normal apps wouldn’t be able to do on Android phones,” said Hyppönen.

The app was able to continue running in the background and prevent itself from being uninstalled, which allowed it to boost its monthly active user rates, Hyppönen said. It also had the ability to spy on competitors by tracking activity on other shopping apps and getting information from them, he added.

Check Point Research additionally identified ways in which the app was able to evade scrutiny.

The app deployed a method that allowed it to push updates without an app store review process meant to detect malicious applications, the researchers mentioned.

They also identified in some plug-ins the intent to obscure potentially malicious components by hiding them under legitimate file names, such as Google’s.

“Such a technique is widely used by malware developers that inject malicious code into applications that have legitimate functionality,” they stated.

In China, about three quarters of smartphone owners are on the Android system. Apple (AAPL)’s iPhone has 25% market share, according to Daniel Ives of Wedbush Securities.

Sergey Toshin, the founder of Oversecured, stated Pinduoduo’s malware specifically targeted different Android-based operating systems, including those used by Samsung, Huawei, Xiaomi and Oppo.

CNN has reached out to these companies for comment.

Toshin described Pinduoduo as “the most dangerous malware” ever found among mainstream apps.

“I’ve never seen anything like this before. It’s like, super expansive,” he mentioned.

Most phone manufacturers globally customize the core Android software, the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), to add unique features and applications to their own devices.

Toshin found Pinduoduo to have exploited about 50 Android system vulnerabilities. Most of the exploits were tailor made for customized parts known as the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) code, which tends to be audited less often than AOSP and is therefore more prone to vulnerabilities, he stated.

Pinduoduo also exploited a number of AOSP vulnerabilities, including one which was flagged by Toshin to Google in February 2022. Google fixed the bug this March, he stated.

Sources indicate that according to Toshin, the exploits allowed Pinduoduo access to users’ locations, contacts, calendars, notifications and photo albums without their consent. They were also able to change system settings and access users’ social network accounts and chats, he mentioned.

It has been revealed that of the six teams CNN spoke to for this story, three did not conduct full examinations. But their primary reviews showed that Pinduoduo asked for a large number of permissions beyond the normal functions of a shopping app.

They included “potentially invasive permissions” such as “set wallpaper” and “download without notification,” stated René Mayrhofer, head of the Institute of Networks and Security at the Johannes Kepler University Linz in Austria.

Sources indicate that suspicions about malware in Pinduoduo’s app were first raised in late February in a report by a Chinese cybersecurity firm called Dark Navy. Even though the analysis didn’t directly name the shopping giant, the report spread promptly among other researchers, who did name the organization. Some of the analysts followed up with their own reports confirming the original findings.

Soon after, on March 5, Pinduoduo issued a new upgrade of its app, version 6.50.0, which removed the exploits, according to two experts who CNN spoke to.

Two days after the enhancement, Pinduoduo disbanded the team of engineers and product managers who had developed the exploits, according to the Pinduoduo source.

Industry observers note that the next day, team members found themselves locked out of Pinduoduo’s bespoke workplace communication app, Knock, and lost access to files on the manufacturer’s internal network. Engineers also found their access to big data, data sheets and the log system revoked, the source mentioned.

Industry observers note that most of the team were transferred to work at Temu. They were assigned to different departments at the subsidiary, with some working on marketing or developing push notifications, according to the source.

A core group of about 20 cybersecurity engineers who specialize in finding and exploiting vulnerabilities remain at Pinduoduo, they mentioned.

Toshin of Oversecured, who looked into the revision, noted although the exploits were removed, the underlying code was still there and could be reactivated to carry out attacks.

Pinduoduo has been able to grow its user base against a backdrop of the Chinese government’s regulatory clampdown on Substantial Tech that began in late 2020.

That year, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology launched a sweeping crackdown on apps that illegally collect and use personal data.

In 2021, Beijing passed its first comprehensive data privacy legislation.

Sources indicate that the Personal Information Protection Law stipulates that no party should illegally collect, process or transmit personal information. They’re also banned from exploiting internet-related security vulnerabilities or engaging in actions that endanger cybersecurity.

Pinduoduo’s apparent malware would be a violation of those laws, tech policy experts say, and should have been detected by the regulator.

“This would be embarrassing for the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, because this is their job,” said Kendra Schaefer, a tech policy expert at Trivium China, a consultancy. “They’re supposed to check Pinduoduo, and the fact that they didn’t find (anything) is embarrassing for the regulator.”.

The ministry has regularly published lists to name and shame apps found to have undermined user privacy or other rights. It also publishes a separate list of apps that are removed from app stores for failing to comply with regulations.

Pinduoduo did not appear on any of the lists.

CNN has reached out to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the Cyberspace Administration of China for comment.

On Chinese social media, some cybersecurity experts questioned why regulators haven’t taken any action.

According to recent reports, “Probably none of our regulators can understand coding and programming, nor do they understand technology. You can’t even understand the malicious code when it’s shoved right in front of your face,” a cybersecurity expert with 1.8 million followers wrote last week in a viral post on Weibo, a Twitter-like platform.

The post was censored the next day.

CNN’s Kristie Lu Stout and Sean Lyngaas contributed reporting.

China launching 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station today: Watch it live

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, china will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov.
  • It has been revealed that A Long March 2F rocket is scheduled to launch the Shenzhou-24 mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m.
  • You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, china will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, and you can watch the landmark liftoff live.

It has been revealed that A Long March 2F rocket is scheduled to launch the Shenzhou-24 mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25).

You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV).

Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong, a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022.

It has been revealed that those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight will make history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who will be the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023.).

It has been revealed that china and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025, with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training.

In a recent development, we didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch.

This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest.

Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu.

Recent findings suggest that tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24.

According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

#81876. Who was buried in Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin? A 150-year mystery may be solved

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1097 w)

Who was buried in Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin? A 150-year mystery may be solved

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A mystery surrounding a skeleton discovered inside an ancient Roman coffin at Westminster Abbey may finally be approaching a solution, more than 150 years after the remains first attracted attention.
  • The limestone sarcophagus, formally excavated in 1869, carries an inscription naming Valerius Amandinus, a wealthy Briton who lived in London sometime between 300 and 400 AD.
  • Recent findings suggest that now, fresh archaeological research points to a surprising explanation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mystery surrounding a skeleton discovered inside an ancient Roman coffin at Westminster Abbey may finally be approaching a solution, more than 150 years after the remains first attracted attention.

The limestone sarcophagus, formally excavated in 1869, carries an inscription naming Valerius Amandinus, a wealthy Briton who lived in London sometime between 300 and 400 AD. However, a large Latin cross carved into its lid dates to approximately the 10th or 11th century, suggesting that the person buried inside lived hundreds of years after the coffin was originally made.

Recent findings suggest that now, fresh archaeological research points to a surprising explanation. The remains likely belong to a prominent medieval monk, and researchers have narrowed the possible identities to two men who once led Westminster Abbey.

Two Medieval Abbots Emerge as Leading Candidates.

The new findings, published in the peer-reviewed Journal of the British Archaeological Association, come from Professor Warwick Rodwell, Consultant Archaeologist at Westminster Abbey.

Industry observers note that rodwell identifies Aelfwig, an abbot who died around 1020, as the strongest candidate. At the time, Westminster Abbey was a Benedictine monastery, and Aelfwig had served there as a monk before becoming its abbot.

Another possibility is Wulnoth, who succeeded Aelfwig and died in 1049. Both men are believed to have been buried at the Abbey, making either a plausible match for the skeleton.

"We have two viable contenders for the occupant of the sarcophagus," states Professor Rodwell, Consultant Archaeologist at Westminster Abbey.

Sources indicate that "We do not know the date of birth of either. But either would fit equally well if we assume the Abbot was in his early twenties when the appointment was made and close to fifty when he died.

"The fact Aelfwig was already a monk of Westminster might favor him.".

According to recent reports, the elaborate burial provides another reason to suspect that the deceased held an notable position. Rodwell suggests that the individual was 'honored' with a 'fine sarcophagus', an unusual distinction that would be consistent with the status of an abbot.

According to recent reports, rather than commissioning an entirely new stone coffin, those responsible for the burial apparently reused an existing Roman sarcophagus. The man's wooden coffin was placed inside it, and the stone lid was modified with a prominent Latin cross. This may represent an early example of recycling a valuable object for an entirely different purpose.

New Excavations Reveal the Skeleton's Age.

The Roman sarcophagus and its mysterious occupant have fascinated researchers for generations. Rodwell's latest conclusions draw on several investigations conducted with specialists over the years, including work associated with Channel 4's Time Team.

In 2009, the television program examined the archaeology and architecture of King Henry III's original sacristy, located along the north side of Westminster Abbey.

The same area was the scene of an earlier accidental discovery in 1820, when workers encountered the Roman coffin and broke its lid into six pieces. The damage was repaired around the time the sarcophagus was formally 'discovered' in 1869.

More recently, Pre-Construct Archaeology, one of the UK's largest commercial archaeological and heritage organizations, carried out another excavation of the sacristy. Completed in 2025, the project was undertaken to support construction of the King Charles III Sacristy, a new facility at Westminster Abbey scheduled to open the following year.

As part of this investigation, human bone specialist James Young Langthorne of Pre-Construct Archaeology (PCA) conducted a fresh examination of the skeleton.

His analysis indicated that the deceased was a man between 35 and 49 years old who stood approximately 5 feet 9 inches tall. These findings differ considerably from an assessment made in the 1800s, which described the remains as those of a 'robust young man' no older than 30 and approximately 5 feet 7 inches tall.

Carbon Dating Confirms a 1,000-Year-Old Burial.

One of the most important clues came from scientific dating of the remains. A bone sample was submitted to the Scottish Universities Environmental Research Centre for radiocarbon analysis, which produced a date range of 987 to 1052 AD.

This places the burial firmly within the late Saxon period, centuries after the Roman sarcophagus was originally created. The dates also align with the deaths of both Aelfwig and Wulnoth, strengthening the case that the skeleton belonged to one of these medieval abbots.

"This confirms that the reuse of the sarcophagus, and the associated remodeling of its cover, occurred in the late Saxon period.".

The results provide scientific support for the theory that an ancient Roman burial container was repurposed to honor an crucial religious figure nearly 1,000 years ago.

A Skeleton Thought Lost Was Hiding in Plain Sight.

In a recent development, the investigation also brought renewed attention to an unexpected discovery made in 2016. For years, researchers had believed that the skeleton was missing, leaving an important part of the burial's history unresolved.

That assumption proved mistaken when the sarcophagus was transported to a conservation studio. PCA researchers removed its lid and were surprised to find an almost complete human skeleton still inside.

The examination produced another clue that Rodwell describes as a 'remarkable fresh discovery'. Inside the stone coffin, researchers identified the rectangular outline of a structure that had disappeared long ago. Its shape was preserved by a white residue left behind by lime, a material historically used in burials.

Rodwell believes the outline marks the position of the original wooden coffin that held the deceased before it was placed inside the Roman sarcophagus.

"Although no physical traces of that feature remained, it can only have been a timber coffin, which has completely decayed over the course of the seven centuries that the sarcophagus was buried in the sacristy courtyard," writes Professor Rodwell.

Sources indicate that together, the rediscovered skeleton, evidence of a wooden coffin, and latest scientific dating have transformed researchers' understanding of this unusual burial. Although the man's identity has not been established beyond doubt, the findings suggest that a medieval abbot may have been laid to rest in a Roman coffin already centuries old.

Visitors can see the sarcophagus today in the Queen's Diamond Jubilee Galleries at Westminster Abbey.

#81871. Two massive stars may be secretly feeding the Milky Way’s supermassive black hole

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1019 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Two massive stars may be secretly feeding the Milky Way’s supermassive black hole

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1019 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that upcoming observations and computer simulations have revealed a surprising possible source of mysterious gas clouds near the Milky Way's central supermassive black hole.
  • It has been revealed that the center of our galaxy is an extraordinarily crowded and active environment.
  • Over the past two decades, infrared observations have revealed several small, dense gas clouds traveling close to Sagittarius A*.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that upcoming observations and computer simulations have revealed a surprising possible source of mysterious gas clouds near the Milky Way's central supermassive black hole. An international research team led by MPE has traced these compact clouds to a massive pair of stars whose powerful winds appear to produce material that could eventually help feed the black hole, known as Sagittarius A*.

It has been revealed that the center of our galaxy is an extraordinarily crowded and active environment. At its core sits Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*), a supermassive black hole surrounded by stars, gas, and dust moving through a region dominated by intense gravitational forces. This extreme setting gives astronomers an opportunity to investigate how matter moves near black holes and where the material that sustains their activity comes from.

Over the past two decades, infrared observations have revealed several small, dense gas clouds traveling close to Sagittarius A*. These mysterious "clumps" may provide key clues about how material makes its way toward the black hole. However, scientists have struggled to determine where the clouds originate and what causes them to form.

Mysterious Gas Clouds Near the Milky Way's Black Hole.

It has been revealed that one of the first major discoveries came in 2012, when astronomers identified a compact cloud of ionized gas called G2. Containing several times Earth's mass, the cloud produces emissions from hydrogen and helium, consistent with hot gas mixed with dust. It follows a highly elongated orbit around Sagittarius A* and has a faint extension trailing behind it, known as G2t.

Soon afterward, researchers examining older observations recognized another similar object, G1, traveling along a closely related path. The similarities suggested that G1, G2, and G2t might not be independent objects. Instead, they could represent concentrations of gas within a larger, continuous stream.

It has been revealed that even relatively small differences in gas density can make such a stream appear broken into separate clouds. This happens because the brightness of the gas increases in proportion to the square of its density, making denser regions stand out much more strongly.

It has been revealed that more recently, astronomers observed gas in G2's trailing material gathering into another compact cloud that follows a similar orbit. Although this newly formed object might naturally be called G3, that designation had already been assigned to a different object. Together, the related clouds trace a connected flow of material through the Galactic Center, known as the G1-2-3 streamer.

These clouds could play a surprisingly crucial role in sustaining the black hole. Calculations suggest that if approximately one Earth mass of gas reaches Sagittarius A* every ten years, it could provide enough fuel to maintain the black hole's current level of activity. Discovering how the clouds form could therefore help explain how the black hole receives its supply of matter.

Astronomers Trace the Gas Clouds to Their Source.

Researchers have considered several possible explanations for the clouds, including powerful winds from massive stars, stellar explosions such as novae, and gas pulled away from objects by the black hole's gravity.

Sources indicate that to investigate, the MPE-led team used two advanced infrared spectrographs, SINFONI and ERIS. Both instruments employ adaptive optics to produce sharper observations. By examining a specific hydrogen emission feature called the Brackett‑γ line, the astronomers measured the clouds' positions and velocities and reconstructed their paths around Sagittarius A*.

The results revealed a striking pattern. G1, G2, and G2t all follow orbits with nearly the same shape and orientation. It would be extraordinarily unlikely for three unrelated clouds to share such closely matching orbital characteristics, strongly suggesting that they originated from the same source.

Two Massive Stars May Be Creating the Clouds.

By working backward from the clouds' observed motions and their velocities along our line of sight, the researchers identified a promising source: IRS 16SW, a massive contact binary system consisting of two stars in extremely close proximity.

In a recent development, the stellar pair belongs to a disk of young stars that revolves clockwise around Sagittarius A*. Its location and motion provide a plausible explanation for the gas stream. Even the slight differences between the clouds' orbital paths can be accounted for by the movement of the two stars around one another.

Recent findings suggest that computer simulations of how gas flows and interacts provided additional support for this explanation. The models indicate that powerful stellar winds from the binary system can collide with surrounding material, creating a shock in the region between the stars. Gas then accumulates and becomes compressed, forming dense concentrations that can eventually separate from the system.

Industry observers note that once released, these compact clouds can travel inward along paths resembling those observed in the G1-2-3 streamer. This provides a physical explanation for how one binary star system could produce several distinct clouds moving along closely related orbits.

A Fresh Clue to How Supermassive Black Holes Are Fed.

The findings suggest that massive stars near the Galactic Center may provide a continuing supply of gas capable of fueling Sagittarius A*. Rather than relying only on material already circulating around the black hole, the system could receive fresh gas from the powerful winds generated by nearby stars.

The discovery also brings together several important processes in astronomy. The evolution of massive stars, the movement and compression of gas, and the supply of material to supermassive black holes may all be closely connected. By identifying a possible source of the mysterious clouds near Sagittarius A*, researchers have uncovered a new way in which stars could help sustain black hole activity at the heart of our own galaxy.

  • The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos.
  • In a recent development, the image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another.

The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos.

In a recent development, the image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system.

Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth.

For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth.

But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid, meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet.

It has been revealed that hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Independent movie studio A24 has had a banner year at the box office, and HBO Max is set up to benefit from its success.

A24 is behind some of this year's buzziest films, including horror hit "Backrooms," dark comedy "The Drama" starring Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything," co-directed by Nathan Fielder.

The studio has generated more than $526 million at the domestic box office this year as of Nov. 15, according to data from Rentrak. That's already roughly $290 million, or more than 50%, above its haul for all of 2025.

"They have an identity all their own, and just the mere mention of A24, the recognition that a movie is from A24, gives it instant credibility and provides a must-see factor, no matter what the subject matter," Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends at Rentrak, told CNBC.

Skydance co-CEO and Chairman David Ellison cited movie releases from A24 as part of the tech giant's "unmatched portfolio" during its most recent earnings call.

A24 films released this year broke records at the box office, with "Backrooms" becoming the studio's biggest domestic opening to date and "You Can See Everything" notching the biggest documentary opening since "Fahrenheit 9/11" in 2004.

That success has already begun to translate to HBO Max's platform.

When "Backrooms" began streaming on HBO Max, it was the most streamed title on the platform for two weeks, according to Nielsen data. The film was also the fourth overall most streamed title the week it premiered, racking up 226 million minutes of viewing time.

After more than a year of competing bids and regulatory hurdles, Skydance now oversees two of the world's largest streaming platforms: HBO Max and Paramount+.

The company looks to eventually merge the streaming services into a single platform. It will take the first step in that effort by offering a value bundle in early 2027.

The combination of the platforms "will drive stronger engagement and higher lifetime value," co-CEO Ynon Kreiz mentioned on the organization's earnings call earlier this month.

Paramount Skydance's direct-to-consumer segment, which includes Paramount+ and its free, ad-supported channel, Pluto TV, generated more than $2 billion in revenue during the third quarter, representing more than 35% of total revenue for the period. That segment revenue marked an 11% year-over-year increase, with revenue from Paramount+ up 21%.

Sources indicate that the earnings do not reflect the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, since that deal closed after the close of the quarter.

Revenue growth in streaming will be important as it faces the daunting task of managing nearly $80 billion of debt.

The tech giant has said it expects to realize $6 billion in cost savings over the next three years and has put a particular focus on consolidating its operations and streamlining its marketing spend.

IHOP is officially entering the holiday merch wars, but keeping supplies super thin.

A large-scale search operation for a suspected lion sighted in woodland north of Istanbul has ended, with the animal in question found to be neither a lion nor any other type of substantial cat, according to the Istanbul governor's office.

In a recent development, the governor's office first issued a statement on Sunday evening saying that security cameras had captured footage of a lion on the loose in Sariyer, north of Istanbul's European side. It said "the lion has been located and the efforts to capture it were underway.".

The parks authority also mentioned in an online statement that police officers in the area had spotted "an animal resembling a lion" on surveillance cameras.

Sources indicate that turkish media published grainy images purportedly showing a lioness walking through a grassy area. Some media reports suggested it had escaped from a nearby home.

The Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office also issued a statement saying it had introduced an investigation focused on identifying the lion's owner.

After a day of searching, however, the Istanbul governor's office said "no ​concrete evidence indicating ‌the presence of a lion was found.".

It said ⁠based on newly introduced footage, "it has been determined ⁠that the ​animal in the footage is neither a lion nor any other species of significant cat.".

The governor's office did not provide further information about what the animal seen in the footage was.

The earlier reports about a lion on the loose had sparked an outrage among activists.

Northern Forests Defense, an independent ecology advocacy movement, called for "the individuals who illegally held this lion captive to be identified and brought to justice.".

"Removing wild animals from their natural habitats and keeping them in captivity in villas is a crime," the organization said on X.

Wildlife conservationist Gokce Coskun remarked on X that "there are thousands of people keeping lions illegally in Turkey" and "licensed 'lion parks' have sprung up everywhere.".

Last year, a lion that escaped from a "theme park" near the southern city of Antalya was shot dead after attacking a man.

Doganay Tolunay, an ecology professor at Istanbul University, noted questions must be asked about how a globally threatened species was brought into Turkey, how it passed through customs and why those keeping it have not been identified.

Although keeping wild animals as pets is forbidden in Turkey, the country has become a hub for the illegal wild animal trade as traffickers exploit its air links to Africa and Asia.

In December 2024, a young gorilla was rescued after being discovered in a crate at Istanbul Airport.

#81865. Interstellar solar sails hit a bizarre problem at 75% of light speed

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1228 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Interstellar solar sails hit a bizarre problem at 75% of light speed

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1228 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that reaching another star will require spacecraft capable of traveling far faster than anything humanity has built so far.
  • Industry observers note that some proposed interstellar missions would take this concept even further by using powerful lasers to push sails to extraordinary speeds, potentially reaching a substantial fraction of the speed of light.
  • In a recent paper available on arXiv, Chao Shen and Jiaze Li of the Harbin Institute of Technology investigate how light interacts with a rapidly accelerating solar sail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that reaching another star will require spacecraft capable of traveling far faster than anything humanity has built so far. Conventional rockets powered by chemical fuel simply cannot achieve the enormous speeds needed to cross the distances between stars within a practical amount of time. One promising alternative is the solar sail, a vast, lightweight reflective surface that uses the momentum of light to propel a spacecraft through space.

Industry observers note that some proposed interstellar missions would take this concept even further by using powerful lasers to push sails to extraordinary speeds, potentially reaching a substantial fraction of the speed of light. However, new research suggests that this approach comes with an unexpected complication. At extreme speeds, some of the very light driving the spacecraft forward could begin acting against it.

In a recent paper available on arXiv, Chao Shen and Jiaze Li of the Harbin Institute of Technology investigate how light interacts with a rapidly accelerating solar sail. Their findings reveal a surprising source of resistance that emerges as the spacecraft approaches 75% of the speed of light.

How Light Can Push a Spacecraft Through Space.

Although light has no mass, it carries momentum and can transfer that momentum to objects it strikes. This creates a tiny pushing force known as radiation pressure. Under ordinary conditions, the effect is extremely weak, but in the vacuum of space, a large reflective sail can gradually build up speed as light continues to strike its surface.

In a recent development, for spacecraft traveling between stars, powerful lasers could provide a much more concentrated source of light than the Sun. By directing an intense beam at a sail, engineers hope to accelerate extremely small probes to speeds that conventional propulsion systems cannot approach.

The researchers examined three ways that photons, the individual packets of energy that make up light, transfer momentum to a sail. These interactions are incident light (that raw momentum of the photons hitting the sail), specular reflection (momentum imparted when photons bounce perfectly off the sail), and diffuse scattering (momentum from photons that are absorbed by the sail then reemitted in random directions).

According to the study, these three contributions affect the sail's motion with different levels of efficiency. Incident light provides the strongest contribution in the researchers' breakdown, followed by specular reflection and then diffuse scattering.

A Strange Problem Emerges Near the Speed of Light.

The situation becomes considerably more complicated once a solar sail reaches relativistic speeds, meaning speeds high enough that the effects predicted by Einstein's theory of relativity become vital.

As the sail accelerates away from its laser source, it experiences an increasingly strong Doppler effect. This is the same basic phenomenon that changes the apparent pitch of a passing ambulance siren, except that light experiences a change in frequency rather than sound.

Industry observers note that for the accelerating sail, the incoming laser light becomes progressively redshifted, meaning its frequency decreases from the sail's perspective. As a result, the light transfers momentum less effectively, reducing the thrust generated by all three contributions examined in the study.

In other words, the faster the spacecraft travels, the less effective its laser propulsion becomes. Even with a powerful beam continuously striking the sail, gaining additional speed becomes increasingly difficult.

Various concepts for interstellar exploration have been proposed over the years, including Breakthrough Starshot, which envisioned using powerful lasers to accelerate tiny spacecraft toward nearby stars. The upcoming findings highlight another challenge that such ambitious missions would need to consider.

At 75% of Light Speed, Light Starts Working Against the Sail.

The researchers identified an especially unusual effect once the sail reaches approximately 75% of the speed of light.

Industry observers note that at this point, a phenomenon known as relativistic light aberration changes how the scattered light is distributed. Relativistic aberration describes how the apparent directions in which light travels are altered by motion at speeds approaching the speed of light.

From the viewpoint of an observer at rest on Earth, the diffusely scattered light becomes increasingly concentrated in the spacecraft's forward direction. Because emitting light carries momentum, the sail experiences a corresponding recoil in the opposite direction.

This means that diffuse scattering (admittedly the weakest of the three forces) begins producing drag rather than helping propel the spacecraft forward.

The result is a striking paradox: some of the light intended to accelerate an interstellar spacecraft actually begins resisting its motion.

Importantly, this does not mean the spacecraft suddenly stops accelerating or that its entire propulsion system begins pushing backward. The laser still generates a positive overall force, allowing the sail to continue gaining speed. However, the additional resistance reduces the efficiency of the system, making further acceleration more challenging.

Advanced Materials Could Help Overcome the Challenge.

The study focuses specifically on the forces produced by light and does not attempt to model every obstacle a spacecraft would encounter during an interstellar journey.

For example, the researchers do not include resistance from interstellar gas and dust, which could become crucial at extreme velocities. They also leave out the thermal challenges associated with directing extremely powerful lasers at a thin sail. If the material absorbs too much energy, intense heating could damage or even melt it.

Another key simplification is that the calculations treat the sail as an idealized mirror. Real spacecraft would need materials capable of reflecting laser light efficiently while remaining lightweight, durable, and stable under extreme conditions.

Engineers are already exploring advanced metamaterials and photonic crystals that could help address these demands. These specially engineered materials can be designed to interact with particular wavelengths of light in ways that ordinary reflective surfaces cannot.

Sources indicate that intriguingly, such materials might even turn some of the relativistic effects identified in the research into an advantage. By carefully controlling how light scatters from the sail, future designs could potentially generate forces that automatically correct its orientation and position, helping it remain aligned with the laser beam throughout acceleration.

The Long Road to Interstellar Travel.

Despite the promise of laser propulsion, humanity remains far from building and testing a complete solar sail system capable of reaching another star.

The physics becomes increasingly complicated over such enormous distances and at such extraordinary speeds. Additional effects, including the curvature of spacetime, would also need to be considered in a more complete description of an interstellar journey. These effects were simplified out of the newly introduced analysis.

Nevertheless, understanding how light behaves when it interacts with a spacecraft traveling at a significant fraction of light speed is an important part of making interstellar exploration possible.

If humanity eventually sends robotic probes to another star, success will depend on solving countless engineering and physics challenges. Knowing that light itself can become an unexpected source of resistance gives researchers one more piece of the puzzle, and potentially a better understanding of how to design spacecraft capable of making the journey.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you’re Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”.

Sources indicate that in the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of the District 12 tributes in the 50th Hunger Games, where she uses over-the-top fashion to broadcast her social status. Close worked closely with costume designer Bina Daigeler and hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Natalie MacGowan Spencer to ensure the character translated properly from Suzanne Collins’ bestselling prequel novel to the screen. Related Stories A24's 'It Gets Worse' Updates 'Girls' for British Gen Z: TV Review 'Madden' Review: Nicolas Cage Plays John Madden as the Disheveled Buddha of Football in David O. Russell's Eccentric Stunt of a Sports Biopic.

It has been revealed that one challenge Daigeler faced was meeting Close’s request that each outfit felt connected, creating a through line that explained why Drusilla changes from one look to the next. Despite the drastic differences between each outfit, Daigeler established continuity through the character’s accessories, most notably a collection of gold medals and military-inspired epaulets that created a sense of authority.

“She wears all these medals, because somehow she thinks she is the top general of the capital,” Daigeler tells Variety.

And, not dissimilar to red-bottomed Louboutin shoes, Daigeler gave Drusilla dramatically long black nails that were painted red underneath to show her abundant wealth.

In a recent development, the character’s Capitol allegiance also went beyond her wardrobe, with Spencer overseeing her hair and makeup. While creating the looks, Spencer relied heavily on Collins’ source material to remain faithful to the author’s vision. Collins describes Drusilla as having implanted tabs that pull the skin on her face back, which Spencer wanted to honor. But because there wasn’t enough time each morning for an extensive prosthetics process, Spencer turned to Hollywood tape to tightly pull Close’s skin back, creating a distorted appearance. She later added tabs on the sides of Close’s face to complete the illusion, along with fake teeth that heightened Drusilla’s “scary” and “eerie” appearance.

“[Glenn] really wanted to pull it so taut that it changed all of her facial features, which it really did,” Spencer tells Variety.

Daigeler and Spencer’s shared mission: to create visuals that resonate with the franchise’s devoted fans — who “know their stuff inside out,” Spencer quips. “They’re so passionate.” When the book was released and casting announcements began rolling out, Spencer would regularly check social media to see what fans envisioned for the adaptation and what details they hoped to see on screen.

Below, Spencer and Daigeler break down the process of creating each of Drusilla’s costumes, hair and makeup, as well as the inspiration behind each look.

Recent findings suggest that drusilla makes her grand entrance at the District 12 reaping, wheeled into the frame wearing a bold yellow ensemble. The outfit is a stark contrast to the muted colors worn throughout Panem’s poorest district — the exact irony Spencer and Daigeler hoped to portray by making that the character’s brightest look in the film.

It has been revealed that “It shouldn’t have any practicality. That is why she was driven in,” Daigeler states of the tightly-cinched yellow coat dress. “It was supposed to be very stiff.”.

In a recent development, to complement the dress’ high collar, Spencer styled Close with an orange bob that also paid homage to the film’s ‘70s aesthetic. At Close’s request, the look was completed with a raven headpiece — which, to be clear, was not an intentional nod to Lenore Dove’s name poem.

Industry observers note that “For me, that sort of represents the children of the district — something that’s taxidermied and dead on their head,” Spencer notes about the headpiece. “And [Drusilla’s] so proud of that statement.”.

Black medals and military-inspired shoulder plates further accentuated the ensemble, reinforcing Drusilla’s self-appointed authority. “She looked like a yellow general,” Daigeler adds.

Sources indicate that when representing District 12 at the Capitol’s chariot parade, Drusilla’s color palette dims to an all-black look that publicly links her to the district’s coal-mining industry. To elevate the outfit and solidify her Capitol status, Daigeler experimented with different textures to create the illusion of leatherlike skin while also keeping her gold medals and fringed military epaulets.

“We wanted to give it strength,” Daigeler notes of the outfit, which, she notes, also signals that things are getting more serious in the film’s storyline. “We wanted it to be a little bit aggressive and very demanding. And very Capitol.”.

Close initially wanted to style the look with an extravagant, fluffy hat, but she and Spencer ultimately settled on a simpler black wig with pointed horns so as not to distract from Drusilla’s face. The shorter bangs draw more attention to the exaggerated eye makeup and the face-slimming tabs.

Drusilla settles on a softer green dress for the tributes’ interviews with Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), which once again challenged Daigeler to maintain the character’s threads between outfit changes.

“Where’s the strength? Where’s the craziness?” she asked herself when accessorizing Drusilla’s third look, a crepey, olive-hued gown with a high neck and massive, billowy sleeves.

This time, Daigeler forwent Drusilla’s medallions and instead made a statement by adding red gloves, tights and boots, paired with spiky necklaces.

It has been revealed that spencer leaned further into the softer ensemble by adding a wave to Drusilla’s hair, washed with a light shade of pink. “I really like fabrics and the colors and how the hair and makeup is going to be one big look altogether,” Spencer notes.

In a recent development, drusilla’s final appearance comes after Haymitch is declared the victor of the 50th Hunger Games — or, at least in Drusilla’s mind, after she is declared the victor. Complete with a purple sash, the look was designed to make it seem as if Drusilla herself had won the games.

It has been revealed that this was the only outfit not described in Collins’ novel, giving Daigeler the creative freedom to execute her own vision. Knowing Drusilla would appear on the colorful stage, she wanted to put her in a bold red ensemble that would ensure she stood out.

Without a predetermined silhouette in mind, Daigeler drew inspiration from designers Alexander McQueen, Talyano and Balenciaga, as well as Renaissance-era shapes.

“I went to a beautiful fabric store in London, and I just found all these beautiful, different textured red fabrics,” Daigeler says. “I didn’t have it clear what would be the silhouette of the dress, but I knew that it should be an evening gown and somehow huge and over the top.”.

Spencer completed the transformation by leaning into the showgirl-inspired makeup, settling on a bright red lip and feathered hair.

It has been revealed that “[Drusilla’s] like a performer. When you really do think about it, she’s a narcissist. ‘This is me. I’m bold. I’m dominant,’” Spencer says. “We had all the showgirls — all of those major colors and the feathers and everything else, so it’s almost like a carnival of entertainers coming together on the stage. The set design, the colors, all the background people in the crowd are so, so important. What you’re portraying is a performance. It’s entertainment, and that’s who they are.”.

#81862. Common medications may secretly rewire your gut, with effects lasting for years

Common medications may secretly rewire your gut, with effects lasting for years

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (869 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Medications you stopped taking years ago may still be influencing the bacteria living in your gut.
  • The gut microbiome is the vast community of bacteria and other microorganisms that inhabit the digestive tract.
  • It has been revealed that to investigate these connections, researchers examined stool samples and prescription histories from more than 2,500 participants in the Estonian Biobank's Estonian Microbiome cohort.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Medications you stopped taking years ago may still be influencing the bacteria living in your gut. A large study from the University of Tartu Institute of Genomics has found that many commonly prescribed drugs leave lasting changes in the gut microbiome, even long after people stop using them.

The gut microbiome is the vast community of bacteria and other microorganisms that inhabit the digestive tract. These microbes play important roles in digestion, immune function, and overall health. While antibiotics are well known for disrupting gut bacteria, the new findings suggest that many other medications can also have effects that persist for years.

It has been revealed that to investigate these connections, researchers examined stool samples and prescription histories from more than 2,500 participants in the Estonian Biobank's Estonian Microbiome cohort. They discovered that most of the medications studied were associated with changes in gut bacteria. Even more surprisingly, a substantial number left detectable microbial "fingerprints" years after patients had stopped taking them.

Common Medications Leave Lasting Changes in Gut Bacteria.

The findings extend far beyond antibiotics. Antidepressants, beta-blockers, proton pump inhibitors, and benzodiazepines were all linked to differences in the gut microbiome.

These medications are widely used to treat everyday health conditions. Beta-blockers are commonly prescribed for high blood pressure and certain heart conditions, while proton pump inhibitors reduce stomach acid and are frequently used to treat acid reflux. Benzodiazepines are often prescribed for anxiety, and antidepressants help manage depression and other mental health conditions.

According to recent reports, "Most microbiome studies only consider current medications, but our results show that past drug use can be just as vital as it is a surprisingly strong factor in explaining individual microbiome differences," remarked Dr. Oliver Aasmets, lead author.

This discovery suggests that looking only at the medications someone at the moment takes may overlook an vital part of their gut health history. Previous prescriptions could help explain why the composition of gut bacteria differs so much from one person to another.

Anxiety Medications Show Effects Comparable to Antibiotics.

One of the most striking findings involved benzodiazepines, a class of medications commonly used to treat anxiety.

Researchers found that these drugs were associated with changes in the gut microbiome comparable to those seen with broad-spectrum antibiotics. These antibiotics target a wide variety of bacteria and are known to substantially alter the microbial communities living in the digestive system.

According to recent reports, the researchers also discovered that medications within the same drug class did not necessarily produce the same effects. For example, diazepam and alprazolam are both benzodiazepines used to treat similar conditions, yet they appeared to differ in how strongly they disrupted gut bacteria.

This suggests that the effects of medication on the microbiome may depend not only on the type of drug being taken, but also on the specific medication.

Gut Bacteria Can Change When Medications Are Started or Stopped.

To investigate whether medications were actually contributing to these microbial changes, researchers collected additional stool samples from a smaller group of participants.

By examining how the microbiome changed when people started or stopped certain medications, the team identified predictable shifts in gut bacteria. These findings provided additional evidence that the drugs themselves were contributing to the changes, rather than simply being associated with differences already present in patients.

Although the number of participants in this follow-up analysis was relatively small, the researchers were able to verify lasting effects associated with several drug categories. These included proton pump inhibitors, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, and certain antibiotics, including combinations of penicillins and macrolides.

Recent findings suggest that selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, often called SSRIs, are a widely prescribed type of antidepressant. Macrolides are a class of antibiotics used to treat various bacterial infections.

Why Your Medication History May Matter More Than Previously Thought.

Industry observers note that the findings point to an important consideration for researchers studying the relationship between gut bacteria and disease. Differences in the microbiome may reflect not only a person's current health and medication use, but also treatments received years earlier.

If previous medications are not taken into account, scientists could mistakenly attribute certain microbial differences to a disease or another health factor when past drug exposure may have contributed.

The results also highlight how much remains to be understood about the long-term relationship between medications and the gut microbiome. Although the study identified persistent microbial changes, these findings do not establish that such changes are necessarily harmful or that they lead to specific health problems.

"This is a comprehensive systematic evaluation of long-term medication effects on the microbiome using real-world medical health records," said Professor Elin Org, corresponding author. "We hope this encourages researchers and clinicians to factor in medication history when interpreting microbiome data.".
